requirements.text: Enable law enforcement agencies to capture defendant and incident information along with supporting paper documents within 48 hours of arrest.
Enable magistrates to electronically review request(s) for counsel and submit request(s) for counsel within 24 hours of the indigency hearing.

Enable the Office of Attorney Appointments to review request(s) for counsel and process request(s) for counsel as soon as possible, but not later than the end of the first working day after the date on which the Office of Attorney Appointments receives the request for appointment of counsel.
Enable law enforcement agencies to be notified that the request for counsel has been denied within 24 hours of the denial.
Enable the appointed attorney and Defendant to be notified that an appointment has been made within 24 hours of the appointment.
Enable an appointed attorney to review appointments and capture the date and type of first contact with the defendant no later than the end of the first working day after the date of the appointment.
Enable an appointed attorney to capture the date and time of the first in person visit with the defendant, as appropriate.
Enable the Office of Attorney Appointments to be notified when first contact by an appointed attorney is not made by the of the first working day after the date of the appointment.
Enable the appointed attorney and Office of Attorney Appointments to be notified that the District Attorney has accepted/rejected the incident and whether charges where added, removed or modified.
Enable the Office of Attorney Appointments to produce comprehensive reporting measurements that reflect compliance with the Texas Fair Defense Act.
Implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to ensure that each actor can only access data necessary for their specific role, and enforce multi-factor authentication for all system access.
All sensitive defendant information and financial records must be encrypted using industry-standard protocols (e.g., AES-256 for data at rest, TLS 1.2+ for data in transit).
The system shall process and record the appointment request within 5 seconds of submission by the Magistrate.
In the event of an external system integration failure, the system shall queue requests locally and provide an automated retry mechanism with notification to the administrator.
Define maximum latency for report generation, e.g., 'All standard reports must be generated within 30 seconds for any selected date range.'
Define integration performance, e.g., 'Data synchronization between the IJIS and the Court Case Management System shall occur with a latency of no more than 5 minutes.'

OPEN: The PRD lacks requirements for audit logging of access and modifications to sensitive case and financial records. - The system shall maintain an immutable audit log of all access, modifications, and deletions of defendant and financial records, including user ID, timestamp, and action taken.

OPEN: There are no defined requirements for system availability, disaster recovery, or data retention, which are critical for legal records. - The system shall maintain 99.9% availability during business hours and retain all indigent defense records for a minimum of 7 years in accordance with state law.

OPEN: The PRD lacks expected transaction volumes or concurrent user counts for the reporting and appointment modules. - The system shall support up to 500 concurrent users and process a peak load of 1,000 appointment requests per day without performance degradation.

OPEN: The PRD lacks expected transaction volume, concurrent user counts, or data retention requirements for the system. - Include a section on system capacity, e.g., 'The system shall support at least 50 concurrent users and process up to 5,000 new appointment requests per month.'
